note: Window agent p1600-p1609, 2 Nov 2026. Four corrections: the 1609 Safavid/Ottoman keyframes (keyframe_overrides/0-1), the Tumed disc over Ming Shanxi (rulings/0), the New Mexico heartland left unowned (events/0).

region.text: the state of New Mexico, the heart of Santa Fe de Nuevo Mexico, 'centered on the upper valley of the Rio Grande', less the 17 cells the Spanish Empire's own 1600 shape keeps

events.note: 'On July 12, 1598, Oñate established the New Spain colony of Santa Fe de Nuevo Méjico'; 'The first capital was San Juan de los Caballeros from 1598 until 1610'. The dossier's own 1598 keyframe gives New Spain the whole province, but the cells of the state of New Mexico were then held by the Spanish Empire and the Spanish Empire's 1600 keyframe drops them, so from 1600 the heart of the province (about 1,067 cells) is nobody's while the rest of the province is New Spain's. This gain hands them to the colony, as the dossier's keyframe and ledger event 2 (1598) already say.

correction.text: the 1609 shape without Kandahar (Mughal until 22 June 1622) and without Iraq (Ottoman until 1624), plus the land the Safavid ledger gained from the Ottomans in 1603-1606 that Cliopatria's 1609 shape leaves to the Ottomans: Tabriz and Persian Azerbaijan (21 October 1603), Nakhchivan (October 1603), Yerevan (June 1604), Ganja, Baku, Shirvan and Shamakhi (June 1606)

keyframe_overrides.why: The 1609 keyframe snap strips 370 cells to nobody (Shirvan 147, Azerbaijan 182, Armenia 80, East Azarbaijan 62 and more) that the ledger gave the Safavids on dated sentences: 'The Safavid army was able to capture Tabriz on 21 October 1603', the Safavids entered Nakhchivan the same month, they 'had already captured Yerevan in June' 1604, and 'Abbas I was able to liberate Ganja, Baku, Shirvan, and Shamakhi in Azerbaijan in June 1606'. The Ottoman 1609 keyframe already gives that land up, so it was left with no owner until 1612. The correction keeps the dossier's own 1609 shape and adds the regions of the ledger's gains.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1609 shape with Iraq restored, without the land the Safavid ledger took in 1603-1606 (Tabriz and Persian Azerbaijan, Nakhchivan, Yerevan, Ganja, Baku, Shirvan and Shamakhi), without the rest of Armenia and Azerbaijan (lost in the Ottoman ledger in June 1604 and June 1606; Karabakh's Khamsa under a Persian protectorate from 1603) and without Tbilisi, Kartli and Kakheti; the rest of the Tabriz disc (Van, Hakkari, the Iraqi Kurdistan edge, West Azarbaijan) stays Ottoman until the Treaty of Nasuh Pasha (1612)

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's correction removes a 250 km disc around Tabriz, which also cuts Ottoman land that the Safavids never took (Van, Hakkari, the Iraqi Kurdistan edge): 171 Ottoman cells went to nobody in 1609. The page has the Ottoman commander withdraw 'to the fortress of Van' after the 1605 defeat. The correction removes exactly the regions of the Safavid ledger's gains of 1603-1606 (the same regions as the corrected Safavid 1609 shape, so the two do not overlap) and the Georgian lands, and keeps the rest until the Treaty of Nasuh Pasha (20 November 1612). [Reviewer, 2 Nov 2026: Armenia and Azerbaijan are subtracted whole again, as in the dossier's own correction. Without them the snap handed the Ottomans 47 cells of Karabakh (Kelbajar, Aghdam, Khojavend, Lankaran, Zangilan and more) that had been nobody's since kingdom-of-artsakh dissolved in 1603: 'In 1603 the Persians established a protectorate over the Khamsa' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principality_of_Khachen), and the Ottoman ledger already loses Armenia (June 1604) and Azerbaijan (June 1606), when 'Abbas I was able to liberate Ganja, Baku, Shirvan, and Shamakhi in Azerbaijan'. Van, Hakkari, the Iraqi Kurdistan edge, West Azarbaijan and the Ardabil edge, Ottoman in 1608, stay Ottoman.]

region.text: Shanxi, which lies south of the Tumed pastures

rulings.why: The Tumed dossier draws a 200 km disc around Hohhot, which reaches 102 cells into Ming Shanxi. The page puts the Tumed pastures 'north of the border with Shanxi, in present-day Inner Mongolia', and after the 1571 peace Altan Khan was a tributary neighbour of the Ming, so Shanxi stays Ming.
